alternatives_listed.reason: Three genuine, distinguishable alternatives: MCS first, pantograph first, forbid the combination in Kconfig; the chosen one is included.

consequences_present.reason: States what changes (when-branch order MCS, pantograph, none in ARCH_CHG_INLET, first true wins) and the trade-off (a both-feature product leaves the pantograph requirement unsatisfied), but names no follow-on work for that unsatisfied requirement.
consequences_present.suggestion: Name the follow-on work for a product with both features, e.g. how the unsatisfied REQ_PANTOGRAPH_CHARGING is reported or handled (gap, Kconfig warning, product review).

context_present.reason: States the problem (Kconfig allows MCS and pantograph together) and the constraint driving it (room for only one high-power charging interface).

rationale_quality.reason: Compares options (MCS for long-haul trucks over pantograph; open Kconfig over forbidding), but rests on unstated assumptions: 'main BEV use case' is asserted while bus products use the pantograph, and it does not say why a future pantograph truck needs the MCS+pantograph combination to stay allowed.
rationale_quality.suggestion: Ground 'main use case' (which product lines / volumes) and state explicitly why forbidding the combination would block the future pantograph truck (e.g. it will also carry MCS).

summary: Clear context and alternatives; consequences omit follow-on work for the unsatisfied pantograph requirement; rationale leans on unstated assumptions.
